content.title: Where to watch the Tigers starting today: Detroit SportsNet releases list of providers
content.text: TigersUpdated: Mar. 26, 2026, 9:07 a.m.Published: Mar. 26, 2026, 9:06 a.m.If you received FanDuel Sports Detroit last season, you probably won’t need to do anything. But check to verify. (photo by Evan Woodbery, MLive.com)Evan Woodbery, MLive.comBy Evan Woodbery | ewoodber@mlive.comSAN DIEGO -- If you’ve been wondering — and worrying — about how you’re going to watch Detroit Tigers baseball in 2026, you finally have some answers. And they arrive just in time: first pitch against the Padres is at 4:10 p.m. Eastern today at Petco Park.Detroit SportsNet, the new home of the Tigers and Red Wings, will be available on all or almost all of the providers that previously carried FanDuel Sports Detroit. That includes Comcast/Xfinity (Channel 1253), Charter/Spectrum, traditional DirecTV and DirecTV Stream (Channel 663).Visit this website to see if your provider is on the list. If you have a smaller provider, enter your zip code and then select the provider from the drop-down list. If you received FanDuel Sports Detroit last season, you probably won’t need to do anything. The channel may have shifted slightly, but it should still be in the same general neighborhood.If you’re a cord‑cutter within the Tigers TV market who doesn’t have a traditional cable or satellite provider, you’ll need a Detroit SportsNet (DSN) subscription, which unlocks Tigers broadcasts inside the MLB app.For out‑of‑market fans, nothing has changed. The best option remains MLB.tv (streaming) or MLB Extra Innings (through your provider). Below are more questions and answers we’ve addressed previously.What is Detroit SportsNet, and why did the Tigers and Red Wings make the switch?DSN is the new joint streaming and broadcast platform for the two pro sports teams owned by the Ilitch family. It provides in‑market access to both Tigers and Red Wings broadcasts under a single subscription — $19.99 per month or $189 per year.Key points:Tigers games will stream via the MLB app, beginning Opening Day (March 26), for fans who subscribe to DSN.Red Wings games will join DSN starting with the 2026–27 NHL season.The broadcast teams remain unchanged: Jason Benetti and Dan Dickerson will handle play‑by‑play duties, with Dan Petry and Andy Dirks as primary analysts.The Red Wings’ specific streaming platform for 2026–27 has not yet been announced, but team officials say on‑air talent and production will remain intact.The move came after Main Street Sports Group — operator of the FanDuel Sports Network channels — faced the same financial struggles that led to the 2023 bankruptcy of its predecessor, Diamond Sports Group. Late payments pushed the Tigers and eight other MLB clubs to terminate their contracts and shift to MLB‑supported distribution.Q: I watched Tigers games last year through my cable or satellite package. Do I have to do anything?Probably not. But check this link to verify that your provider will carry DSN.If your provider carries DSN, but you don’t see it on your TV, verify that you are subscribed to a tier or package that includes sports networks like DSN.Cord‑cutters who watched games last year using FanDuel’s streaming product will need to purchase a Detroit SportsNet subscription to watch games on the MLB app.What’s the difference between MLB.tv and Detroit SportsNet?MLB.tv is for out‑of‑market viewing. If you live in the Tigers’ TV territory, an MLB.tv subscription does you no good: Tigers games will be blacked out.Detroit SportsNet is for in‑market streaming and unlocks all local Tigers broadcasts inside the MLB app.It’s worth emphasizing: Downloading the MLB app is free and doesn’t require a subscription to MLB.tv. If you live in Michigan and only want to stream the Tigers, you need DSN, not MLB.tv.Where do I actually watch DSN? Does it have its own app?For cable and satellite subscribers, DSN has been assigned a “channel” just like Fan Duel Sports Detroit.For streamers, no separate DSN app exists (at least not yet). DSN broadcasts will live inside the MLB app. Once you subscribe to DSN, Tigers’ broadcasts will be unlocked inside the app.What is the MLB app?You can find it on the app store on your phone or tablet. If you have a smart TV, you can add it to your home screen, just like Netflix or Disney or other services. The MLB app is free and can be used even if you don’t pay for any subscriptions. But if you live in the local market and you want to watch the Tigers, you’ll need a DSN subscription to unlock broadcasts in the app. I’m an out-of-market Tigers fan. Do I need Detroit SportsNet?No.If you live outside the Tigers’ broadcast region, MLB.tv works exactly as before. You do not need DSN.Offers to “add local broadcasts for your area” apply only to the team in your home market — not the Tigers.So, say you live in Phoenix, and you want to watch the Tigers. A normal MLB.tv subscription works just fine. If you want local Diamondbacks broadcasts, you can bundle that with your MLB.tv subscription.Also, some providers offer “MLB Extra Innings.” It works just like MLB.tv, but it’s for people who watch on traditional TV rather than stream. Can in-market Tigers fans bundle DSN and MLB.tv?For now, no.Unlike most MLB‑operated regional models, DSN covers two teams (Tigers and Red Wings), complicating bundling. There is no discount for combining DSN and MLB.tv.As it stands, if you live in Detroit and want to watch the Tigers and, say, the Angels, you’ll have to subscribe to both DSN and MLB.tv. There is no bundling discount available at this time.Q: I paid for a year-long streaming subscription to FanDuel Sports Network Detroit. Now that it no longer carries Tigers games — and soon won’t carry Red Wings games — can I get my money back?You’re not alone. There are plenty of fans who signed up for a full year, including those who were on auto‑renewal and got charged for another year just before the changes were announced.Your FDSN Detroit subscription does not transfer to Detroit SportsNet, so you must cancel your FDSN plan and request a refund for the unused portion.The easiest way to do this is through FanDuel Sports Network’s customer support form:A customer service agent told me the following:Full or pro‑rated refunds are offered, but only if you purchased the subscription directly through FanDuel Sports Network’s website.If you bought it through an app store (Apple, Roku, Google Play, etc.), FanDuel cannot process the refund. You’ll need to request it from the platform you paid through.If your subscription was purchased directly through FanDuel, you have two options:Receive a pro‑rated refund but keep access through May 1, 2026, or until the NHL season ends.Cancel immediately and receive a pro‑rated refund, losing access right away.Keep in mind: with app stores, you may have to actively request a refund; simply canceling may not trigger one.10 Tigers games you can watch for free this season — and where to find themDetroit Tigers sign minor-league infielder released by BravesOpening Day could be warmest in decades.
